walk.title: Solve it: turn a WhatsApp order into clean cargo
walk.sample: Mrs Adebayo · 2 crates of tomatoes + 1 big bag of tatashe · Tuesday afternoon · 14 Ring Road

steps.say: A real order arrived on WhatsApp on Monday morning. We'll turn it into JSON any automation could use, then work out the total from paths.
Read it the way a machine would need it: who, what, and where and when. And Tuesday after Monday the fifth is the sixth of October.
show: Where/when: address, day, time of day

steps.say: Choose a type for every field before writing anything. The phone is a string, because you never add phone numbers, and that keeps the country code safe.
Products go in an array, because an order can have any number of them. Paid is a true or false, and notes is null on purpose.
Now write it. Customer and delivery become objects, and each product gets a stable sku, so later steps don't care how someone spells tatashe.
Money stays a plain number with no naira sign or commas, and the date is ISO, so nothing can be misread.
Test it in the lab. Tap a path and see the value and its type. Remember, counting starts at zero.
Try items two. There are only two items, so it comes back empty. That's the most common beginner bug.
Calculate the total from paths: each quantity times its price, plus the delivery fee.
Only when we show it to Mrs Adebayo does it become thirty-five thousand five hundred naira with a sign. Inside the data it stays a number.
Spreadsheets can't hold a list in one cell, so we flatten it: one row in Orders, one row per item in Order items, linked by the order ID.

walk.end: Right types, clear paths, a total you can trust. In Module 0.5 you'll make AI produce exactly this JSON from any messy message.
